title: relay
description: v0.2 device-model entity: a binary on/off load, one per channel, published under renewvan/relay/<id>/<property>. `state` is the output as commanded and latched, published only after the physical output changed; it does NOT mean the load is energised (no feedback sensor: a stuck relay or blown fuse is not detected). `name` is the optional, retained, human label and the only label on the wire. Command topics (unretained, not separate schema files): `renewvan/relay/<id>/set` carries JSON `true` or `false` only (no toggle: it is not idempotent); `renewvan/relay/<id>/name/set` carries a JSON string (five segments, so it never matches the four-segment entity topic). A consumer treats `state` as unknown whenever the owning Driver's health is not `online` or is absent. After any restart every channel is off; the Driver alone owns boot state and the hub never re-asserts a desired state. One source per id: two Drivers must not publish the same renewvan/relay/<id>/... topic. A Driver that stops publishing an id it knows about publishes an empty retained payload (no value). See docs/adr/0013-writable-relay-and-its-wire-contract.md.

driver.description: Optional, retained. The key of the Driver publishing this instance: the <driver> segment of renewvan/<driver>/info, published as renewvan/relay/<id>/driver. Same slug rule as driver-info.schema.json. Identity field. A consumer must tolerate it being absent (a Driver that predates it) and then attributes the instance to every Driver whose info `publishes` lists 'relay'.
